When most people are unemployed, and living on some form of welfare, the question will occur to those who dole out the money: do we need them? What happens when it's very apparent that most of the population is a burden? When every job requires a human, all kinds of humans of all different abilities and temperaments have their place. What happens when 47% or more of the population has no place? Is the right thing to perpetually sustain this underclass of people who do nothing? Maybe. It's not their fault that they have no purpose. The jobs they are perfectly suited for, that have existed in some form throughout all human history, are now gone. So do you sustain them forever, perpetually dragging along an increasingly large and atrophied mass, or is that the point where eugenics or genetic engineering kick in?

I know nobody wants to talk about this. It's very uncomfortable. Surely this has crossed someone's mind though. It doesn't seem plausible to me that those with resources will voluntarily re-allocate huge percentages of those resources to people who don't work, from the near future until the end of time. You can make all the rules and laws you want, but that isn't going to fly for very long. Corporations already have so much influence over government. What reason is there to believe that governments will make the right moves when the times comes, or do anything at all? Governments are already fucking this up. Every $15 minimum wage law accelerates the move to automation. I have no confidence in governments to fix this.

I just don't see this smooth transition into a basic income utopia. I see rioting, starvation, death, and destruction. I hope I'm wrong. Even if it all goes well, and there's a smooth transition, and basic income works exactly as intended, what happens to people? They have their income, but what do they do? Do they watch TV all day? Do they turn to drink, and violence, and cause problems? Do they fall into deep depression? I mean, it's nice to think everyone will just pick up hobbies and live happily ever after, but I live around humans every day and I'm not so sure. Some may use the opportunity to better themselves, but I think most people will turn to sludge in front of the TV, or become drunks, or start looking for trouble. Even if they don't, is the vast majority of humanity destined to sit on the sidelines? It's all very troubling. As much as I'd love to not have to work and be able to spend all my time on my hobbies, this doesn't seem like a very bright future for humanity. I see no reason to be enthusiastic about people becoming kept animals, fed and cared for by people who only pay for it under the threat of violent revolt.

I can't let my fantasies of unlimited free time blind me to all the different ways this could play out. It seems very naive to me to think that basic income will definitely happen, at the exact right time, in the exact right way, and it will work perfectly, and there will be no ill effects. I won't waste too much energy on pointless worrying, but I will definitely try to prepare for as many potential futures as I can. I'm sure not betting my life on the government coming to the rescue when I need them.
